subject: Streaming response stall - hosted inference advisory
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Caldwell <ben.caldwell@beaconpulse.com>, BeaconPulse Support <support@beaconpulse.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming response stall - hosted inference advisory

Hi Ben / BeaconPulse team,

We're seeing a subset of streaming generation requests from eu-west-1 intermittently stall during the response-streaming phase. Impact: some in-flight streams pause for ~6–20s before resuming. This affects approximately 3% of streaming requests for models with long prefixes (>512 tokens) between 08:45–09:05 UTC. Non-streaming (batch/text generation) endpoints are unaffected.

What we've done so far:
- Identified correlated error logs on the streaming I/O path tied to the new multiplexing handler deployed in last night's rollout.
- Shifted traffic away from the affected worker pool and enabled fallback to the legacy streaming path for new sessions.
- Opened an incident (IR-2028-03-21) and paged SRE.

Customer-facing impact / guidance:
- You may see paused streams for long-context requests; clients should tolerate a short stall and not retry immediately (retries can cause duplicate responses).
- We're prioritizing restoring the stable streaming path; a follow-up update within 30 minutes or sooner.

I'll loop in SRE with technical details and a timeline shortly. Apologies for the disruption — we know streaming behavior is core to BeaconPulse's UX and are treating this as high priority.

Chloe Martin
Senior Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_streaming_timeline.csv (timeline stub)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Caldwell <ben.caldwell@beaconpulse.com>, BeaconPulse Support <support@beaconpulse.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming response stall - hosted inference advisory

Chloe — thanks for the heads up. Quick tech notes and immediate mitigation plan: 

Root cause (prelim): regression in the streaming multiplexing handler introduced in 2028-03-20T23:40 UTC deployment. Under high prefix-KV-cache pressure the multiplex handler can block on an edge NVMe read when a cache miss hits a retired shard; that blocks the streaming task and holds the socket open while scheduling backfills.

Mitigations enacted:
- Disabled multiplexing path for active eu-west-1 workers (traffic shifted to legacy streaming path) — this reduced observed stalls by ~90% for incoming requests.
- Restarted two worker groups (wg-11/wg-12) running the new runtime to clear stuck tasks.
- Prepared a small patch to add a non-blocking backfill path (ops_patch_023.diff) — will coordinate fast rollback if any regressions.

Next steps (ETA):
- Roll out ops_patch_023 to a single canary group in 10 minutes; monitor p95/p99 for streams.
- If stable after 15 minutes, roll to remaining groups. Full restoration expected within 45–60 minutes unless we see new anomalies.

Please send an external-facing note summarizing the temporary fallback and expected timeline; I'll provide the concise technical blurb for a postmortem.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
SRE (Runtime)
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming response stall - hosted inference advisory

Hi Ben — thanks, and sorry again for the interruption. Final update and next steps: 

What we did:
- Disabled the new multiplexing handler and shifted affected sessions to the legacy streaming path at ~09:55 UTC.
- Deployed ops_patch_023 to canary at 10:05 UTC, validated for 20 minutes, then rolled to remaining eu-west-1 workers by 10:40 UTC.
- Observed p99 streaming stall incidence fall to baseline (<0.1%) by 10:50 UTC.

Impact on latency: legacy streaming path can add ~50–100ms to p95 for long-context sessions vs the multiplexing handler in normal conditions; this is well within typical client tolerances and avoids the multi-second stalls.

SLA/credits: if the final postmortem shows this incident meets our credit policy windows we'll apply the appropriate usage credits. I'll include an explicit calculation in the postmortem.

Attachments and follow-ups:
- Attached: incident_streaming_timeline.csv (minute-level timeline) and ops_patch_023.diff (patch notes + rollback guardrail).
- Postmortem and RCA will be delivered by EOD tomorrow (IR-2028-03-21). Status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/IR-2028-03-21

If you'd like an immediate sync to walk through the timeline and our fix, I can set up a 30-min bridge this afternoon.

Thanks for your patience — we value BeaconPulse's partnership and will ensure the post-incident steps reduce recurrence risk.

Chloe Martin
Senior Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
